precepts.text: The world is divided into ten parts and ten parts of it are gone already. That was during the time of Ezra; understand we are in the last days and the clock is ticking. Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people. Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right. If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage. If the home front is not right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people?
precepts.point: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: he sees what is about to happen and he prepares for that. But the simple pass on, and are punished. Somebody watching this class is taking notes, saying that is some good stuff, and then will immediately close their Bible, go home, and proceed to be a demon. You saw the evil, but you are not hiding.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself”. Knowing the time, we had better prepare ourselves. Ezra was told: “For the world is divided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it are gone already, and half of a tenth part: And there remaineth that which is after the half of the tenth part.”

That was during the time of Ezra. Understand that we are in the last days; the clock is ticking, brethren. We have leadership able to show us what is going to come to pass, and we just saw Daniel 3 come to life before our eyes. Babylon is going to burn. If you're smart, you'll get ready.

“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”. Knowing the time, we must set our houses in order. Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right and fix their stuff.

If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage; that is the first place. If the home front isn't right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people? How are we going to inherit what the Lord has prepared for us if we are not taking this Bible seriously? The simple take notes, say that's some good stuff, close the Bible, go home and proceed to be a demon. They saw the evil but they aren't hiding, and they pass on and are punished.

precepts.text: If so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive, and after death ye shall obtain mercy. We got to be transformed in the renewing of our minds.
precepts.point: The Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt be turned into another man. You don't believe that you could become a whole different person; the scripture says you can.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.text: I led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to mount Sinai, where I held him by me a long season: the forty days and forty nights. He told Moses many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times, the beginning, the middle, and the end; that is how Moses wrote the first five books, and how he saw even his own end before the promised land.
precepts.point: All these things happened unto them for ensamples, and are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. The acts of the apostles continue; we are learning from our forefathers the same way the congregations in Asia Minor did.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. That baptism is Moses teaching us the laws of God, and teaching us the gospel, teaching us about Christ, because Moses spoke with Christ. Christ said, “Before Abraham was, I am”: it was Christ that spoke directly to Moses. We often think the gospel only begins in the book of Matthew. It does not.

Ezra shows it: “And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”. That mount is Sinai, and the long season is the forty days and forty nights. “And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

Moses was shown the beginning, the middle and the end of times; that is how he was able to write about it in the first five books. He even saw himself not entering the promised land. “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

“That thou lay up in thy heart the signs that I have shewed, and the dreams that thou hast seen, and the interpretations which thou hast heard: For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.”

So when Paul says our fathers “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ”, it is plain: the Israelites in the wilderness were taught the gospel through Moses, who had been with Christ on the mount. Those things are written “for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”; we learn from our forefathers the same way the congregations scattered in Asia Minor did, and the acts of the apostles continue.

precepts.text: Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people. Your house cannot be in order while your head is not. Check your own thoughts and temptations before correcting your wife, son, or daughter; then your obedience is fulfilled and you can revenge disobedience.
precepts.point: Having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience when your obedience is fulfilled. Brothers want to be on the Saturday night specials casting out demons in the street, but you cannot revenge disobedience until there is no impediment to sin left in your own spirit, your household, and your children.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Some of our people can't wait: they want to be part of the war in the streets, casting out demons, getting their names on the Saturday night specials: brother, get a good angle of me, I want my video to go up Saturday. But here's the stipulation: when your obedience is fulfilled. That means there is no impediment left in your spirit to commit sin; you are walking straight in your spirit, your household, with your children, blameless. Then you can go out and correct your people.

That is what the Apocrypha says: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. First set your house in order. Your physical house can't be set in order if your spiritual house, meaning your damn head, is not in order. You haven't even checked your own wicked thoughts, your own actions, your own temptations, and you are trying to correct your wife, your son and your daughter.

Set your head in order; then you can set your house in order; then you can reprove your people. That is when your obedience is fulfilled, and you can revenge all disobedience, because you checked it first within yourself. We want to play warrior, to look good, while there are demons all up in us that we have not corrected yet.

precepts.text: He hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, to know how the world was made and the operation of the elements, the beginning, ending, and midst of the times. God showed Solomon how the world was created, where air comes from, the spirit in fire, why the ocean never overflows. The greatest king who ever walked the earth almost was consumed by what he knew, and we have not been shown ten percent of it. Anyone who says he knows everything in the Bible is a fool; the Bishops teach more today because more of the spiritual world opens to them as time goes by.
precepts.point: These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide. The prophets did not show Israel everything, but what we have is enough to make the kingdom. Nothing is wrong with reading other books, but only one book gets you out of here; the scriptures are your number one focus.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

precepts.why:
God held Moses by him a long season and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Ezra was not the only one; God showed Solomon the same. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”.

God showed Solomon how the world was created, from the beginning, when he said let there be light. He showed him how the elements operate: water, air, fire. You breathe the air but do not know where it comes from; ask Solomon. There is a spirit in fire: a little fire can consume a whole place; ask Solomon how. Everything runs to the ocean, yet the ocean never overflows; ask Solomon why. Christ said you cannot even count the hairs on your head. Those things are too heavy for us, but God showed them to Solomon.

The scripture says Solomon had more knowledge than any king before him or after him, the greatest king who ever walked this planet. He knew so much that at the end the knowledge almost consumed him. And he saw the beginning, the middle and the end of time, just as Moses did.

So if a young man says, I know everything in the Bible and there is nothing anybody can teach me, you are a fool. You can spend your lifetime in this book and still not master it. Bishop Nathanyel was not teaching back then the way he teaches today; as time goes by, more of the spiritual world opens to the Bishops. We have not been shown even ten percent of what was shown to Solomon. The waters are rising; just be patient.

precepts.text: I took it and drank, and my heart uttered understanding, wisdom grew in my breast, and my spirit strengthened my memory.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
When the books of Jerusalem were burned, the Lord told Ezra not to worry, and gave him the cup: “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That last part is the point. God needed something to work with. The Spirit had to access Ezra's memory so that he could rewrite the records. It is like the movie Limitless: the pill opened his memory all the way back, so he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So if you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and you pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the Spirit comes and there is nothing in there: no memory to access and bring to your mind. Wisdom and knowledge can only be the stability of your times if the word has been put in you first, so give the Lord something to work with.

precepts.text: The preacher was wise and set in order many proverbs.
precepts.point: Set thine house in order and reprove thy people. Order your own life first, then you can reprove others.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Set thine house in order and reprove thy people. Order your own life first, then you can reprove others.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

precepts.text: Yet greater evils than those which thou hast seen happen shall be done hereafter.
precepts.point: Neither party is coming to fix things. Work on getting yourself right.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
Christ said “Take heed that no man deceive you”, and then: “ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.” Nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom, famines, pestilences and earthquakes: “All these are the beginning of sorrows.” That is the time we are living in right now: the beginning.

Ezra shows it is only the beginning: “For yet greater evils than those which thou hast seen happen shall be done hereafter.” Greater evils. The things you see taking place on the earth are only the beginning. It is not going to get better, and it is not going to go away. The Democrats are not going to come into office and change anything and make it better. God says it is the beginning of sorrows.

“For look how much the world shall be weaker through age, so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.” The older the world gets, the weaker it becomes, and we are at the end of it right now. The evil is war, death and destruction, and it is going to increase.

So when you see these things, do not be troubled and worried about what is taking place. The world has changed and it is not going to be the same. Work on getting yourself right, and prepare for what is coming.

precepts.text: I have multiplied visions and used similitudes by the ministry of the prophets: the prophets spoke in parables, proverbs and dark sayings as well.
precepts.point: And these shalt thou hide are the dark sayings: there is more to thou shalt not steal, more to not mingling the seed, more to the fringes, and the animal sacrifice itself is the Messiah.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Moses was shown the secrets of the times and the end; that is how the land carried the name Rameses in the writing.
precepts.point: Rameses was the king at the time Israel left Egypt, and Moses wrote the first five books of the Bible; he wrote the place under the name of his own day. In the bush the Most High manifestly revealed himself to Moses, showed him the secrets of the times and the end, the beginning to the end, and the words were written again with Esdras.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

Moses wrote the first five books of the Bible, and the Most High showed him the secrets of the times and the end, the beginning to the end. So when Moses wrote that Joseph placed his father and his brethren “in the land of Rameses”, he wrote the place under the name of his own day: Rameses was the king at the time Israel left Egypt. Goshen and the land of Rameses are the exact same place.

And the words were written again with Esdras, which is how we have them.

precepts.text: The Most High shewed Moses the secrets of the times and the end; that measure of wisdom made his face shine, and some of it he was commanded to hide.
precepts.point: Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
The Most High tells what Moses received in the mount: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

He saw the beginning of the creation, the middle and the end of these times. That measure of wisdom is why his face shone, for a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine.

“These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” Some of that wisdom Moses was commanded to hide and not declare; there is wisdom the Most High gave him that he was not to publish, that we do not even have right now.

precepts.text: The Most High held Moses by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; that is the greatness and the mighty hand Moses praised.
precepts.point: He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Moses besought the Most High: “O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?” The greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. Ezra tells what else it was: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”.

On that mount, held by the Most High a long season, Moses received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep. And more: he “told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” The wondrous things are the prophecies, such as Deuteronomy 28: that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back. The secrets of the times are the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and he was shown the end itself.

All of that stands behind this thanksgiving. When Moses asks what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works, he speaks as a man who has been shown the law, the prophecies and the end.

precepts.text: The Most High held Moses by him a long season on Sinai, shewed him the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded which words to declare and which to hide.
precepts.point: What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy.

note.label: Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness

precepts.why:
What was Moses doing those forty days and forty nights in the mount, neither eating bread nor drinking water? Esdras is told: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times and the end of times. That is why some things Moses wrote, like Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 32 and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy: the Most High commanded him which words to declare and which to hide.

precepts.text: On Sinai the Most High told Moses many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times and the end.
precepts.point: How did Moses know what would happen to the rebellious Israelites in the latter days? The Most High did not only give Moses the ten commandments on Sinai; he told him many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times. That is how Moses wrote Genesis, and that is how he saw ahead of time our people going into captivity again by slave ships, as Deuteronomy 28:68 declares. The prophecies of chapters 32 and 33 are still unfolding to this very day.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

precepts.why:
“For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will befall you in the latter days”. This is heavy: Moses tells the elders and officers gathered before him that evil shall befall the people he is speaking to in the latter days, the last days, because they would do evil in the sight of the Lord and provoke him through the work of their hands. How did Moses know what would happen to the rebellious Israelites in the latter days?

Ezra answers it. The Most High did not only give Moses the ten commandments on Sinai: “I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. He held Moses by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end.

That is how Moses wrote Genesis, and that is how he saw ahead of time our people going into captivity again by slave ships, as Deuteronomy 28:68 declares. He could call heaven and earth to record against Israel because he had been shown the end. The prophecies of chapters 32 and 33 are still unfolding to this very day.

precepts.text: Preparing the heart is setting the house in order and casting off mortal thoughts and the weak nature.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
“Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What preparing the heart means is shown to Ezra himself: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption, Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature.”

To prepare the heart is to set the mind and spirit in order, to examine yourself, to renounce corruption and let go of mortal thoughts, and to put off the weak nature of sin. Ezra did that before he taught statutes and judgments in Israel: he set his own house in order first, and then reproved and comforted the people.

precepts.text: Subdue your own understanding, reform your hearts, and you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.
precepts.point: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” We must understand what we read: this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again. Ezra puts it this way: “if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

A clean heart comes by subduing your own understanding and reforming your heart. The one who does that is kept alive and obtains mercy after death. That is the right spirit David asks the Most High to renew in him.

precepts.text: Set thy house in order, reprove thy people, and renounce corruption; David's house was in disarray, and the sword never left it.
precepts.point: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit. David understood the importance of losing the kingdom; from the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence, and they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” David understood the importance of losing the kingdom. From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence; they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.

Ezra was told, “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”. David's house was in disarray, and the sword never left it. Setting the house in order, reproving the people and renouncing corruption is how the joy of salvation is restored and the free spirit upholds us.

precepts.text: If you subdue your own understanding and reform your mind, after death you shall obtain mercy and be kept alive.
precepts.point: This is the visiting of iniquity in the regeneration; after death comes the judgment, when you reform your mind and subdue your own understanding, and you will be kept alive and obtain mercy.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
The rod and the stripes of Psalm 89 are the visiting of iniquity in the regeneration. Ezra tells how to come through it: “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

After death comes the judgment. If you subdue your own understanding and reform your mind, you will be kept alive and after death obtain mercy. That is the lovingkindness the Most High will not utterly take from David's children even when they break his statutes.

The covenant stands and the mercy is there, but it comes to those who reform their hearts and stop leaning on their own understanding.

precepts.text: Ezra testified the law was burnt, so the Most High put His spirit on Ezra and other men to rewrite the torah.
precepts.point: When the enemy entered the sanctuary and burned everything, they burned our torahs, records, and scrolls, which is why the law is said to be no more.

note.label: Lamentations 2: The Most High Turned Enemy Against Zion

precepts.why:
Her king and princes are among the Gentiles, “the law is no more; her prophets also find no vision from the Lord.” How is the law no more? When the enemy entered the sanctuary and burned everything, they burned our torahs, records, and scrolls.

Ezra testified to it: “For thy law is burnt, therefore no man knoweth the things that are done of thee, or the work that shall begin.” Because the law was burnt, the Most High put His spirit on Ezra and other men to rewrite the torah. That is why Lamentations can say the law is no more, with the sanctuary abhorred, the solemn feasts and sabbaths forgotten in Zion, and the king and princes among the Gentiles.

precepts.text: If so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive, and after death ye shall obtain mercy.
precepts.point: This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. And Christ told him, “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Ezra gives the same thing: “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.” To be born again, a man has to subdue his own understanding and reform his heart.

Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over. Subdue your own understanding, and you shall be kept alive, and after death obtain mercy.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 1

precepts.why: Your two main obstacles in striving to become part of the elect are going to be money and women; every problem we counsel comes back to those two. “Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature”: it is talking about sin, and you know what you are weak to. “And set aside the thoughts that are most heavy unto thee”: money and women; put them thoughts aside. “And haste thee to flee from these times.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: Ezra tells us what Moses saw, in brief. “Where I held him by me a long season”: that long season was 40 days and 40 nights. “And shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”: Christians say God gave Moses Ten Commandments in 40 days and 40 nights; does it take 40 days to give Ten Commandments? Moses saw from Genesis all the way to the second coming of Christ. That’s why when God told Moses he was not getting into the land, Moses didn’t bug out: he saw his resurrection; he saw it all. So Moses is going to tell us everything right now in this song.

points: The Lord said, this information I am showing you is exclusive. Do not give it to everybody.

And when thou hast done, some things shalt thou publish, and some things shalt thou shew secretly to the wise. These are the secrets of the Most High. Everybody is not going to know everything we know. That is how the Lord wants it.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature. Those mortal thoughts are the old habits you created: old thoughts that turned into actions, that turned into habits, that turned into characteristics.

The weak nature is your comfortability. I am used to doing it like this; that is just me. That is the lie you tell yourself. That weak nature is stopping you from being the Proverbs 31 woman that listens to her husband, or the husband that guides his house manfully. Some take the easy way out: no, you are scared to lead your own house. Being nice, brothers will tolerate you, but they will not respect you. You have to break the cycle of comfortability and make yourself uncomfortable doing what you are not used to, because you are trying to get somewhere you have never been. If you are not trying to get there, you will end up destroying yourself through bashfulness.

As we grow in the body, we grow in the truth. Sometimes the Lord brings you to a certain place, and now is the time you get taught: I let you get this far, but you cannot go further until you are okay with getting uncomfortable to break those weaknesses.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: The Lord revealed himself to Moses in the bush, held him by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times. He commanded him: these words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide. Some things Moses hid; he wrote them in parables and similitudes, so everybody cannot understand it. Only the wise can understand it.

They that shall be born afterward, who shall admonish them? That is talking about us today. For thy law is burnt: at that time the Bible was burnt. When you read Nehemiah and Ezra, it tells you our forefathers were not keeping tabernacles or the laws; they grew up in Babylon for 70 years, and the scrolls were destroyed. No man knew the things that God did, like delivering us out of Egypt, and the wars of the Lord. But Ezra knew; he was brought up in the law.

Ezra asked the Most High to send the Holy Ghost into him, and I shall write all that hath been done in the world since the beginning, which were written in thy law, that men may find the path, and that they which will live in the latter days may live. That is how we are able to find the path today: we all came together because we heard the word of God.

Ezra took the five men that were ready to write swiftly, and the Lord lit a candle of understanding in his heart. Ezra was up there 40 days, the same way Moses went up to mount Sinai 40 days, and wrote back everything word for word that Moses gave us. His heart uttered understanding, wisdom grew in his breast, and his spirit strengthened his memory.

The spirit strengthened his memory: that is what the Holy Spirit does. A scripture you read two years ago just comes to your mind in the heat of battle at camp. But it cannot strengthen your memory if you have nothing in your memory. Ezra read the whole Bible many times, so his memory was able to be strengthened. Some of you brothers need your memory strengthened: put something in it.

In 40 days they wrote 204 books. Today we have 80. Remove the New Testament, which came afterwards, and we hold 53; from the 204 that leaves over 150 books missing from the Old Testament from the time of Ezra all the way up to today.

The first that thou hast written, publish openly, that the worthy and unworthy may read it: that is the law; everybody has to learn the law. But keep the seventy last, that thou mayest deliver them only to such as be wise among the people: for in them is the spring of understanding. There were 70 books with some heavy stuff in them that only wise men could read.

Those 70 books, the Most High made it where we do not have them today, because some things in them we are not supposed to know; it would mess with some of our minds. What we do have is enough to get the kingdom: all the laws are there, and the prophecies of what is going to take place. And in the teacher's opinion, some of those books the leadership of Rome has in the Vatican, deep down in the archives.

points: Now therefore set thine house in order. Get your house straight. Do not worry about everybody else right now. When you come in to serve the Lord, get your house together, get everybody right in your house.

And reprove thy people. Before you go out to reprove the people and tell them what they are not supposed to be doing — because then you go home and your wife is in pants. You are telling sisters, get out of the pants, sister, you wicked, but then you go home and your wife is wearing pants and she has got her finger in your face.

It starts in your house. Your little girls, your little boys that you have got in your house — you are the example to them. Especially you men. You men set the tone in your household, period. If the tone is out of order, it is your fault. Back in the 1920s, you see how the black man was sitting down in the chair with that serious, austere face. Everything revolved around the man. Nowadays everything revolves around the children and the woman. When the kids come before you, you wonder why you are not getting any play at the house.

Comfort such of them as be in trouble. You are supposed to not only reprove them but comfort them when they are in trouble. Comfort them through the scriptures, with understanding, with wisdom. That is what we have got to do.

All of us have been out of order, all of us have done wickedness, all of us have done something that is worthy of death. People have been dead for it. But Christ died for us so we can get it right. And guess what — it is that much harder now, because by Christ dying for you, you have got grace and mercy. There is no excuse. It is harder now. He said death by pain, because he gave you time to repent, he gave you time to get it right over and over and over again. When Christ comes back and you try to pray then, it is too late.
